# Independent audit: limiting contact rows and labeled boundary defects

Audited `candidate 8ba63f3af7e6943f`, Sections 1–6. **PASS in the stated finite-label, uniform-source-core scope.** No repair is needed. The source correctly retains a possibly nonzero boundary defect and does not infer its exclusion from ordinary deepestness or from a surface stress.

## 1. Finite touching-plane compactification

The positive-current-weight contact theorem supplies one continuous gradient at each source. Positivity of a touching plane on the fixed-radius own ball bounds its continuous slope by L_i/r_s. The sampled maximum array of L_j−c_ij.X is concave by actual anchored inclusion. Its finite base support LP is feasible at the source; the fixed constraint matrix and bounded right-hand sides give a bounded minimum-norm base slope, including when the source base is a projection vertex. There is no unsupported boundary-base supergradient assertion.

Every chosen touching majorant A_ij is at least L_j on the sampled set, and its affine row expectation is L_ij. The same row has L expectation L_ij. Thus A_ij=L_j almost everywhere on its own row. The minimum V_j of all these majorants is bounded between L_j and A_ij there, and therefore equals L_j on every row. The exact positive target density dm_j/(M_j L_j) makes equality hold throughout each sampled interior. Both functions are finite-PL continuous, so equality extends to the sampled boundary as well. This argument remains valid when a label's positive weight tends to zero; it is used at each finite index before passing to the limit.

The fixed number of bounded planes gives uniform convergence on a common ambient compact set after a subsequence. Log normalization, the uniform maximum bound, and positive fiber volumes bound every fiber maximum below. The usual concave inball/layer estimate then supplies logarithmic uniform integrability and strict positivity of the limit on all sampled interiors. It supplies no positive boundary floor and no inverse-density uniform integrability.

## 2. Exact limiting measure and moments

All probability rows have weak subsequential limits on the limiting actual mixed set. Compact support passes their physical first moments. Uniform sampled parameter convergence and the positive lower source values pass the L moments. The same lower source values bound the total target inverse mass by 1/l_*.

Passing L_j nu_j=dm_j/M_j against continuous tests is valid because L_j converges uniformly and the masses of nu_j are bounded. Thus L nu=dm/M. On every set where L is bounded away from zero this identifies nu with dm/(M L); all remaining mass is a positive measure zeta supported where L=0. In particular the limiting inverse density is integrable, but it may have smaller mass than nu. The source's equations (10)–(11) are the correct exact decomposition and the correct missing zeroth and full first moments.

Each limiting active majorant still has zero nonnegative row defect A−L. Its contact relation survives even on the boundary defect, where A=L=0. Base barycenter preservation forces the entire row, including its defect, into the source's minimal base face. None of these statements deletes the boundary measure.

## 3. Original rows and gradient labels

The weights L_j/L_ij converge uniformly, so the original-volume rows converge to (L/L_i)rho_i. They remain probabilities and their sigma mixture remains exactly dm/M. The zero-L defect contributes nothing to this original-volume identity.

The row mean formula follows directly from the affine contact plane A_i(w)=L_i+a_i.(w−Y_i):

    E_bar_rho_i w−Y_i=Cov(rho_i) a_i/L_i.

The covariance includes any zero-L boundary mass. There is no reason for this vector to vanish.

For every surviving sigma_i>0, the original row is absolutely continuous with respect to mixed volume, of positive total mass. Two source-active planes with different continuous gradients would put that entire row in a hyperplane of zero d-volume in every sampled fiber. This proves unique continuous source gradients even though the tilted row itself may now have a singular part. The proof correctly uses the original row for this step.

Away from the zero set, positive row mass is absolutely continuous and contact with its source plane identifies the target continuous gradient. This yields the labeled tilted equations (15) with the explicit labeled measures zeta_i. At a boundary crease the source label must be retained, and the source does so. Multiplication by L removes these terms only for the original label masses, equation (16). Original first moments still contain covariance terms in equation (17). The nonnegative gradient-norm defect in (18) has the correct sign.

## 4. Scope and checks

This theorem does not assume or prove that the selected sources are deepest; that is separate geometric information in its application. The explicit truncated-triangle example in `candidate 1b1d5e313c1943d1` shows why inverse uniform integrability cannot be inserted into this proof. Conversely, that example does not decide whether full body-minimum/critical-cap information can eliminate zeta.

Reran `work/math-venv/bin/python supporting computation verify_contact_row_boundary_defect_identities_defect_transport.py`: **1,840 exact checks PASS**. These finite checks verify the reweighting and moment identities; the plane compactness and measure decomposition above were independently checked analytically.
